proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to CIB's (COMI) own shareholders was 82,238,852,000 EGP for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, up from 55,196,394,000 EGP in 2024 — an increase of roughly 27,042,458,000 EGP, or about 49% year-on-year. Total net profit for the year was slightly higher (82,258,815,000 EGP in 2025 vs 55,256,732,000 EGP in 2024), meaning the small difference is allocated to non-controlling interests. Net interest income, the bank's core revenue driver, grew from 91,064,222,000 EGP to 107,699,631,000 EGP over the same period, supporting the profit growth.

For your portfolio: you already hold 250 COMI shares worth 32,000 EGP, and your cash is 20,000 EGP, giving a total portfolio of 52,000 EGP. COMI already represents about 61.5% of that total, which exceeds the 50% single-company concentration limit. I therefore cannot recommend buying additional COMI shares. Given that your goal is long-run bank income over a 7-year horizon, your medium risk tolerance, and the strong ~49% profit growth demonstrated in the latest results, the most appropriate action is to hold your existing 250 COMI shares. The company's earnings trajectory is consistent with a bank-income strategy, and selling would forfeit that income stream. That said, the evidence covers only two fiscal years of income-statement data; I have no information on dividend policy, capital adequacy, asset quality, or the competitive landscape, so there is meaningful uncertainty about whether this growth is sustainable over seven years. Monitor future reports for dividend announcements and any deterioration in loan quality before considering any further allocation.
